findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State that stall_abort_args only arms the HTTP(S) transport and confirm (or constrain) that the workspace review/tickets remotes and init's tickets_remote are HTTP(S); note the fix is a no-op on ssh://file:// remotes so the 300s exposure would remain.
evidence: stall_abort_args() returns `-c http.lowSpeedLimit=... -c http.lowSpeedTime=...` (git_fetch.py:212-224) — a curl-transport-only knob
gerrit_client.py builds an https `user:token@host` URL (confirmed HTTP transport)
workspace review/tickets remotes come from REBAR_OPCERT_REVIEW_REMOTE_URL / TICKETS_REMOTE_URL env vars (config.py:30-31,43-44) with no scheme constraint
init.py fetch uses `tickets_remote` config (init.py:387,401,422); scheme is unconstrained
Plan asserts all three are 'NETWORK git calls' but does not establish the transport is HTTP for the workspace/init sites
findings.finding: The fix relies on http.lowSpeedLimit/http.lowSpeedTime, which git only honors on the curl/HTTP(S) transport; for the workspace and init sites the remote URL is operator/config-supplied and may be ssh:// or file://, where these keys are silently ignored, making the abort a no-op and leaving the 300s exposure intact.
findings.location: Plan body: bullet list of the three sites (workspace.py:107,124 and init.py:398,419)
scenarios: An opcert deployment configured with an ssh:// review remote — a zero-byte SSH stall still burns the full 300s because low-speed config never reaches the transport
init on a repo whose sync.remote is an SSH URL

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the per-site retry/fail/degrade decision for each of the three fetch sites when a stall-abort fires, rather than deferring it to the executor.
evidence: "a decision about whether to retry"
Three sites (review bot fetch, opcert workspace fetch, init fetch) have different failure semantics but the plan gives no per-site retry/degrade policy
On stall-abort, whether the caller retries, hard-fails, or degrades determines the reliability behavior of each path
findings.finding: The plan says each call site is 'a splice of `*stall_abort_args()` before the subcommand plus a decision about whether to retry' but never specifies the retry decision per site, deferring a real design choice to the executor.
findings.location: Plan body, 'Reuse the seam 12e4 built' paragraph
scenarios: Executor arms the abort but leaves review-bot fetch to hard-fail while init retries, or vice versa, inconsistently
findings.suggested_fix: For each of the three sites, state whether a stall-abort should propagate as a hard failure, retry N times, or degrade — e.g. 'review-bot fetch: hard-fail the review; init fetch: no retry, surface error'.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify, per site, how is_stall_abort() gets the stderr it needs (e.g. capture returncode+stderr instead of _git_ok's bool / check=True) and whether a retry loop is added or the stall is simply surfaced as a fast failure.
evidence: is_stall_abort(stderr) keys on the stderr marker 'operation too slow' (git_fetch.py:227-233)
workspace._git_ok returns bool, dropping stderr (workspace.py:105-106)
workspace._git raises WorkspaceError only on TimeoutExpired, not on a stall-abort non-zero exit
gerrit_client fetches with check=True (gerrit_client.py:367-373), which raises before stderr inspection
Plan scopes retry as per-site but gives no mechanism for surfacing stderr / integrating a retry loop into these wrappers
findings.finding: The plan says each site adds 'a decision about whether to retry' and reuses is_stall_abort(), but does not account for the fact that the target sites' git wrappers discard the stderr the detector needs: workspace._git_ok returns only a bool and gerrit_client uses check=True (raising CalledProcessError before stderr can be inspected). The snapshot retry loop is not part of the reusable seam, so retry/stall-detection must be re-plumbed per site, which the plan leaves unspecified.
findings.location: Plan body: 'each call site is a splice of *stall_abort_args() before the subcommand plus a decision about whether to retry'; AC line 2
scenarios: Implementer splices the -c args but the fetch still fails on the first stall because the wrapper never inspects stderr to retry, or the test for 'dribbling remote is not aborted' cannot be wired because the wrapper returns only a bool
